findings.text: the promoted-count assertion compares two committed artefacts, the receipt's number and the archive's mask, so a regression that counts the whole mask in nova/equilibrium/display_flux.py leaves it green until the receipt is regenerated; the earlier review recorded the same gap and it is unchanged.

the nearest-promoted bound fits the archive's own spline and never constructs a display map or reads a display_flux field, so no display_flux regression can redden it and the 0.2 bound is stated with no justification for its size.

the repaired polished-saddle check sits inside `if display.saddle_converged:`, so a build that stops converging skips the assertion entirely and the test still passes; making convergence a precondition rather than a branch would let the check fail on that regression too.

the brief asks a red control per new check and only the mask-tail, saddle-offset and caption controls are recorded; the polished-saddle distance and the promoted count carry none, and the fragment itself concedes the promoted-count row's red is the mask-tail test failing rather than a red on that assertion.

`_label_defects` is a third implementation of a figure label-defect count that benchmarks/mast_centroid_solve_panels.py:1395 and benchmarks/diiid_forward_gs_match.py:3695 already carry; no owner module exists to extend, so the three copies will drift independently.

the slow committed-panel test this node edits is recorded in the fragment as hitting its 3300 s ceiling and failing, so the repairs made inside it carry no green run; the same capabilities are covered by the fast tests, but the edits in that test are unverified.
the commits field lists 7 shas for a range holding 8, omitting 122de5110 whose addition f9debe44f then replaced, so a reader reconciling the manifest against the diff finds one unexplained commit.
